article.title: What Colors Go With Burgundy? Outfit Pairings That Work
article.meta_description: What colors go with burgundy? Get the best neutrals, accent colors, shoes and metals, plus easy outfit formulas for work, weddings and weekends.
article.h1: What Colors Go With Burgundy? Outfit Pairings That Work
article.body_html:
Burgundy goes best with cream, navy, grey, camel, blush pink, forest green, mustard and dusty blue. It also works with black and denim if you keep some contrast in the outfit. Below you will find the pairings, the reasons they work and outfit formulas for women and men.

The quick answer: colors that go with burgundy

Burgundy is a deep, muted red with brown or purple in it, so it behaves like a rich neutral. It sits comfortably next to both light and dark shades. A one-glance guide:

Pair burgundy withThe lookEasy example
Cream or ivorySoft, rich, polishedBurgundy knit, cream trousers
NavySmart, classicNavy blazer, burgundy shirt or knit
GreyUnderstated, versatileGrey coat, burgundy scarf or jumper
Camel or tanWarm, autumnalCamel coat over a burgundy dress
Blush pinkTonal, romanticBurgundy skirt, blush top
Forest or olive greenRich, classic contrastOlive jacket, burgundy tee
MustardBold, warmMustard scarf with a burgundy coat
Dusty or light blueCooler, freshLight blue shirt, burgundy chinos
White and denimCasual, everydayBurgundy jumper, white tee, mid-wash jeans

Know your burgundy first

Burgundy comes in two broad versions, and the best partners shift slightly between them.

  • Warm burgundy (oxblood, brownish, brick-leaning) pairs beautifully with camel, olive, rust, mustard, cream and gold.
  • Cool burgundy (wine, plum-leaning) pairs well with navy, grey, icy or dusty blue, blush, white and silver.

Depth matters too. A very dark burgundy behaves almost like black, so it needs a lighter partner to stand out. A brighter, more saturated one is already making a statement, so quieter neutrals around it work better. To test a combination, hold the pieces together in daylight rather than under indoor lighting, which can shift how both colors look.

Neutral colors to wear with burgundy

Cream and ivory

This is one of the easiest pairings. Cream softens burgundy and makes it look expensive rather than heavy. Try a cream knit with burgundy trousers, or a burgundy slip dress under a cream coat.

Navy and grey

Navy and burgundy is a classic, tailored pairing, and it suits offices and dinners. Grey is gentler. Charcoal or heather grey lets burgundy lead without competing with it.

Black

Burgundy and black can look flat if both are dark and matte. Break it up with a lighter element such as a white tee, a cream bag or a metallic accessory. Mixing textures also helps, for example a burgundy knit with black leather trousers.

Camel, tan and brown

Camel is lovely with burgundy because it is clearly lighter. Dark chocolate brown is trickier, because it is close in depth and the two can blur together. If you want to wear them together, add a light layer between them, like a cream top.

White and denim

For weekends, burgundy with white and blue denim is easy and reliable. A burgundy sweater, white tee underneath and mid-wash jeans needs no further thought.

Accent colors that work with burgundy

  • Pink and blush: a tonal look that reads soft and modern. Keep the pink light or dusty rather than hot, which can clash with some burgundies.
  • Forest and olive green: the classic rich combination. It feels most wearable when the green is muted rather than bright.
  • Mustard, gold and rust: warm autumn colors that bring out the brown notes in warm burgundy. Use them in small doses, such as a scarf or a belt.
  • Dusty blue and light blue: a cooler, calmer contrast that suits cool burgundies in particular.
  • Other reds, orange and purple: these can work if you keep one shade clearly dominant and the others as small accents. Burgundy with a brighter red is bolder, and burgundy with plum or berry is smooth and layered. Avoid combining several mid-depth warm brights at once.

Using color theory with burgundy, simply

Tonal looks: wear burgundy with lighter and darker versions of itself, such as a wine knit, berry skirt and rosy-pink scarf. The result looks cohesive and intentional.

Analogous pairings: colors near red on the color wheel, such as plum, berry, rose and rust, sit well together because they share undertones.

Complementary pairings: burgundy is a red, so its opposite is a green-leaning shade. Muted greens like olive, sage and forest are easier to wear than bright ones.

The 60-30-10 idea: use a base color for about 60% of the outfit, a second color for 30% and an accent for 10%. For example, a navy suit (60%), a burgundy knit (30%) and tan shoes (10%). Or a burgundy dress (60%), a camel coat (30%) and gold jewelry (10%).

Shoes, bags and jewelry with burgundy

Shoes

  • Black: sharp and dependable, especially with tailored pieces.
  • Tan or cognac: warm and relaxed, good with navy, denim and cream.
  • Nude or cream: lightens an all-burgundy outfit and visually lengthens the leg.
  • White trainers: good for casual looks.
  • Burgundy on burgundy: works well when the fabrics differ, such as suede boots with a knit.

Gold or silver?

Gold generally flatters warm burgundies, and silver tends to suit cooler wine and plum shades. Rose gold sits nicely in between. Neither is a rule, so choose the metal that looks better against your outfit and complexion.

Bags and belts

Choose a bag in black, tan, cream or a deeper brown to anchor the outfit. A burgundy bag also looks sophisticated with a neutral outfit, such as grey or camel.

Burgundy outfit ideas by piece and occasion

  • Burgundy jumper: with light-wash jeans and white trainers, or tucked into cream trousers with loafers.
  • Burgundy trousers, jeans or skirt: with a cream, grey or light blue top. A fitted top balances wide-leg burgundy trousers, and a longer top softens a burgundy mini.
  • Burgundy dress: for evenings, add black or tan shoes and gold or silver jewelry that matches the burgundy's undertone. A camel or grey coat on top keeps it from feeling too heavy.
  • Burgundy coat or jacket: with a neutral base, such as grey knit and dark jeans, so the coat is the focus.
  • Work looks: a navy or grey suit with a burgundy shirt or knit, or burgundy trousers with a white shirt and a charcoal blazer.
  • For men: a burgundy knit with grey chinos, a white tee under a burgundy overshirt with dark jeans, or a navy suit with a white shirt and burgundy tie or pocket square. Burgundy chinos look sharp with a light blue shirt and brown shoes.

Fabric, texture and season

Texture changes the mood of burgundy. Velvet and satin feel dressy and glossy, while leather reads edgier. Chunky knits are cosy, and cotton or linen blends look relaxed. A single texture contrast, like a matte knit with a shiny bag, keeps the outfit interesting.

In autumn and winter, burgundy works with wool, suede, boots and layers. In spring and summer, go lighter: a burgundy linen shirt with white trousers, burgundy sandals or a bag with a pale outfit, or a burgundy skirt with a blush top. Using it as an accent rather than a base prevents it from feeling heavy in warm weather.

Does burgundy suit you? Skin tone and contrast

Many people find that warmer burgundies suit warmer undertones and cooler wine shades suit cooler ones. If you are not sure which you are, our undertone guide walks through simple tests.

If a shade does not feel quite right near your face, you do not have to give up on it. Wear it as trousers, a skirt, shoes or a bag instead, or put a lighter color like cream or soft blue next to your face. Treat all of this as a starting point rather than a rule, since personal preference matters most.

Combinations to be careful with

  • Tones too close together: burgundy with dark brown, very dark green or deep purple can look muddy because there is little contrast.
  • Too many deep shades: a burgundy top, dark trousers and dark shoes with no break can look heavy.

The fixes are simple: add a lighter layer such as a cream top or white tee, switch to a contrasting shoe like tan or nude, or add a lighter accessory such as a scarf or a metallic piece.

Check your burgundy outfit before you leave

Do a quick mirror check, then take a photo. Photos often show balance and contrast more clearly than a mirror does. If you want a second opinion, FitCheck AI's outfit checker on Android can score a full-body photo or look at your outfit live through the camera. It gives a breakdown of color match, proportion and overall balance, with suggestions like switching shoes or adjusting color contrast. For the best result, use a clear, well-lit, head-to-toe photo that includes your shoes. The feedback is an AI opinion and a starting point, not a professional stylist's verdict, so combine it with your own taste.

faqs.question: Can you wear burgundy with black?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the pairing can look flat if both pieces are dark and matte. Add a lighter element such as a white tee, a cream or tan bag, or metallic jewelry. Mixing textures, like a burgundy knit with leather or satin, also adds depth.

faqs.question: Does burgundy go with navy?
faqs.answer: Yes, burgundy and navy is a classic combination. It works well for smart and work outfits, such as a navy blazer over a burgundy knit. Add a lighter shade like white, cream or light grey so the outfit does not look too dark.

faqs.question: What color shoes go with a burgundy dress?
faqs.answer: Black, tan, nude and cream shoes all work well. Black looks sharp for evenings, nude lengthens the leg and tan suits more relaxed looks. Match your jewelry to the undertone of the dress: gold for warmer burgundy, silver for cooler wine shades.

faqs.question: Is burgundy a neutral?
faqs.answer: Not strictly, since it is still a red, but it behaves like a rich neutral in many outfits. It pairs easily with cream, navy, grey, camel and denim. It tends to work best as a base or main piece, with lighter neutrals or one accent around it.

faqs.question: What is the opposite color to burgundy?
faqs.answer: On the color wheel, the complement of red is a green-leaning shade, so deep or muted greens such as forest, olive and sage sit opposite burgundy. Muted greens are usually easier to wear than bright ones. For a gentler look, pair burgundy with greens in small amounts.

review.notes: The article answers the query directly: a quick answer, a table, neutrals, accents, color theory, shoes and metals, outfit formulas, and pitfalls with fixes. The styling advice is sound and hedged ("not a rule", "starting point"), and it has no invented stats, studies or testimonials. App mentions match APP_FACTS: Android only, free on Google Play, full-body photo or live camera check, color match/proportion/balance breakdown, switching shoes or adjusting contrast, and the photo tip. It also says the output is an AI opinion, not a stylist's verdict. It does not claim iOS, shopping, human stylists, accuracy figures or on-device processing. Minor suggestions: (1) The meta description promises outfit formulas for "weddings", but the body has no wedding section. Either add a short wedding or formal-event line or change the meta description to "evenings" or "dinners". (2) The line "burgundy with plum or berry is smooth and layered" sits a little awkwardly beside the later warning about deep purple looking muddy. Clarify that the warning applies to very dark purple. (3) "Many people find that warmer burgundies suit warmer undertones" is soft and hedged, but it could be reworded as a general guideline. (4) Confirm that the internal links resolve. (5) The CTA is promotional but accurate and appropriately placed.
